memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Some time later Joseph was told, 'Your father is ill.' So he took his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim along with him. When Jacob was told, 'Your son Joseph has come to you,' Israel rallied his strength and sat up on the bed." — Gen 48:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Word reaches Joseph that his father is ill, and he goes at once — and he takes his boys with him. Manasseh and Ephraim are grown men by now, born and raised in Egypt, surrounded by Egyptian culture and Egyptian gods. Joseph deliberately brings them into the room where their grandfather is dying, because he wants them connected to the family God had chosen.

And look at Jacob. Old, weak, lying on a bed — and when he hears Joseph has come, he rallies his strength and sits up. He gathers what little he has left because something important is about to happen. Dying men do not usually sit up. This one does.

There is something moving in both of these decisions. A father who wants his sons to know where they came from spiritually. A grandfather who spends his last strength passing on faith rather than resting.

Faith does not travel down the generations automatically. It is handed over deliberately, by people who make the effort — a parent who brings the children into the room, a grandparent who sits up when it would be easier to lie down.

Timothy's faith lived first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice (2 Tim 1:5). Someone made that effort for him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Who made the effort to pass faith on to you?
2. What are you deliberately handing on to the next generation?
3. Where might God be asking you to spend strength you would rather save?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for those who took the trouble to pass faith on to me. Give me the will to do the same, even when it costs me energy I feel I do not have. Amen.
